clue.text: American composer's dance music style

parts.note: Samuel Barber was an American composer (Adagio for Strings); with the possessive S
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A description of the sort of dance music written by a certain American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a style of close-harmony unaccompanied singing, typically by a quartet.

clue.text: Sex symbol drops back through African capital

indicators.note: the name of the sex symbol loses its back, or last, letter

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe, the screen sex symbol
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A film icon is pictured travelling through a city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Monrovia is the capital city of Liberia in West Africa.

clue.text: Rubbish on top of that ink design

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless rubbish
too means also, in addition, on top of that

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a piece of skin art as rubbish laid over another.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a permanent picture made by putting ink into the skin.

clue.text: Instruction from officer giving discomfort

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
aching, as a noun, is a dull pain or discomfort

explanation.surface: An officer's lessons are said to cause pain to recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaching is teaching or training given to someone, a form of tuition.

clue.text: More than one place on river

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in street names
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: Several sites are located along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural is the grammatical term for denoting more than a single thing.

clue.text: Appealing quality is in entrance area

indicators.note: in puts the word is within the synonym for entrance

parts.note: to entrance, as a verb, is to charm

explanation.surface: A building's appeal is said to lie in its entrance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a doorway but is the verb meaning to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal attractiveness that draws people in.

clue.text: Champion on course to make comeback crows

indicators.note: making a comeback means the horse's name is read backwards

parts.note: Red Rum was the racehorse that won the Grand National three times, a champion on the Aintree course

explanation.surface: A sporting champion returns to the racecourse, oddly beside some crows.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum, the famous British steeplechaser, reads backwards as the collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A murder is the traditional collective noun for a group of crows.

clue.text: Outspoken top dog

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the word for top is spoken out loud

parts.note: a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A blunt-talking champion canine is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is short for a Pekingese, a small long-haired breed of dog.

clue.text: A bit of god-awful back trouble

indicators.note: back says the letters picked are then read in reverse
a bit of says some letters are taken from within the word god-awful

explanation.surface: A spot of dreadful back pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back trouble' looks like a medical complaint; 'back' is the reversal signal and 'trouble' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Play …. with this?

parts.note: Ibsen's play of that title, and also a toy home that children play dolls with

explanation.surface: An unfinished invitation to play with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots stand for the missing word 'dolls': you play dolls with a doll's house, and it is also Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's drama about Nora is named for the miniature toy home it shares a title with.

clue.text: Venture to grab head of state's headgear

indicators.note: to grab means the synonym for venture closes around the other letters

parts.note: to bet is to venture or wager money
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: A gambler tries to snatch a ruler's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a round, flat, soft cap, an item of headwear.

clue.text: Trace grid out one found in magazine

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a grid from a magazine page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a publication, but it is the ammunition chamber of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge, holding bullet and charge, is loaded into a gun's magazine.

clue.text: Italian food recipe a fiddle, mostly

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, 'take'

indicators.note: mostly means the instrument word loses its last letter

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Someone says an Italian dish's recipe is largely a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' reads as a swindle but is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels with a filling, a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Left university to play guitar for several years

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: A student dropped out of college to play guitar for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a period of five years, from the Roman purification ceremony held every five years.

clue.text: Toning down fashion assessment

parts.note: mode means fashion or style
a rating is an assessment or evaluation

explanation.surface: A fashion critic softens their verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderating means making something less extreme, tempering or softening it.

clue.text: Struggling to catch rascal shown on trial

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the rascal and shown come after the trial

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court
an imp is a mischievous rascal
aired means broadcast or shown

explanation.surface: A villain is having difficulty being caught while their trial is televised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' means hear, not seize: struggling to catch what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with impaired hearing has difficulty picking up sounds and speech.

clue.text: Sense criminal isn't attending court

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of isn't are corrupted and rearranged

parts.note: in means present at, attending

explanation.surface: Someone senses an offender has failed to appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate feeling or intuition, a sixth sense.

clue.text: Figure absorbed by my pieces for FT readers?

indicators.note: absorbed by puts the number inside the word my

parts.note: one is a figure, a number
men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A number swallowed up by someone's chess pieces, for the newspaper's audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times's readers are imagined as financiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneymen are financiers and investors, the typical audience of a financial newspaper.

clue.text: Actor in a sporting garment

indicators.note: sporting, as in playing around, means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A performer is wearing some item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as wearing, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A raincoat is a waterproof coat, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Fabulous mount in South America doctor's crossing east to west

indicators.note: to west, in an across clue, means reading right to left, so the whole sequence runs backwards
crossing means the doctor spans the other letter, holding it

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a doctor

explanation.surface: A legendary steed is located in South America, with a vet crossing the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts E inside GP to make GEP; then 'to west' reverses SUSAGEP. 'east to west' looks like one phrase but splits between the two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged horse of Greek myth, a fabled steed.

clue.text: Almost go out, heading for garden, say

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of garden

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Someone almost leaves, heading for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle gutters when it flickers and is on the point of being extinguished.

clue.text: Primarily supercilious, like an aristocrat?

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of supercilious

parts.note: nobby means smart or elegant, like a nob, a slang word for an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A haughty air is said to be typical of the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobby means condescending and superior, looking down on others.

clue.text: Tot somewhere in Blackpool maybe less warm

parts.note: a nip is a tot, a small measure of spirits
Blackpool, a seaside resort in Lancashire, is famous for its piers

explanation.surface: A drink at a seaside resort on a chilly day.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means chilly, so the comparative means colder.

clue.text: Red paper in volume received by fashion house

indicators.note: received by means the letter for volume is taken inside the fashion name

parts.note: Prada is an Italian fashion house

explanation.surface: A book in red paper is delivered to a designer label.
explanation.definitionFit: Pravda was the official newspaper of the Soviet Communist Party, a Red paper.

clue.text: Lots keeping fit love pairing up

indicators.note: keeping means the word for lots holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: many means lots
trim means fit and slim
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Many people stay in shape when love leads to coupling.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is marriage, the union of two people as a couple.

clue.text: Annoy some in room, if flatulent

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wind in a shared room is bound to irritate people.
explanation.definitionFit: To miff is to irritate or offend someone, putting them out.

clue.text: Where races are a tie

definitions.meaning: ... is the Berkshire racecourse, home of Royal ...

explanation.surface: A racecourse is declared a dead heat.
explanation.definitionFit: The English racecourse gave its name to a wide formal cravat worn at the meeting.

clue.text: Loose branch freed, giving pain?

indicators.note: loose means the letters are set free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A branch breaking free and falling causes injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain' looks like hurt; it is the French word for bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is French for bread, so the loaf of France is cheekily defined in its own language.

clue.text: Outgrowth on cereal grass not long

indicators.note: not means the letter for long is removed

parts.note: a lawn is an area of mown grass

explanation.surface: A description of a short growth on a grass plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cereal grass' reads as one botanical phrase; 'grass' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristly hair projecting from the ear of barley and similar crops.
